references.text: God says to Moses: "You cannot see my face, for no one may see me and live." John 1:18 begins with "No one has ever seen God," which directly connects to this statement about God's invisibility. See [ref:2 Mos 33:20|Exodus 33:20].

Moses was allowed only to see God's back, not his face ([ref:2 Mos 33:23|Exodus 33:23]). Even the greatest prophet of the old covenant could not see God directly. It is the only Son who has fully revealed the Father.
Israel heard God's voice at Horeb but saw no form ([ref:5 Mos 4:12|Deuteronomy 4:12]). This underscores God's invisibility, a theme addressed in John 1:18.

Isaiah saw the Lord seated on a high and lofty throne, yet he was overcome with fear because as an unclean man he had seen the King, the Lord of hosts ([ref:Jes 6:1-5|Isaiah 6:1-5]). Even this vision was not a direct sight of God's essence; it is only through the Son that God has been fully revealed.

The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us, and we have seen his glory, "the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father" ([ref:Joh 1:14|John 1:14]). The term "one and only" (μονογενής) is used both here and in verse 18, and the glory of the incarnation is the precondition for the Son to reveal the Father.

God loved the world so much that he gave his "only Son" ([ref:Joh 3:16|John 3:16]). The designation μονογενής is linked here to God's saving action, further clarifying the unique relationship between the Father and the Son that John 1:18 points to.

"No one has ever ascended into heaven except the one who descended from heaven, the Son of Man" ([ref:Joh 3:13|John 3:13]). Only the one who comes from the Father can reveal him, which aligns with the fact that the only Son "who is in the bosom of the Father" has made him known.

Jesus says: "Not that anyone has seen the Father; only the one who is from God has seen the Father" ([ref:Joh 6:46|John 6:46]). This is a direct parallel to 1:18 and confirms that only the Son has direct knowledge of the Father.
Jesus says to Philip: "Whoever has seen me has seen the Father" ([ref:Joh 14:9|John 14:9]). The Son is the perfect revelation of the Father, which is the core message of John 1:18.

"No one comes to the Father except through me. If you had known me, you would have known my Father also" ([ref:Joh 14:6-7|John 14:6-7]). The Son is the only way to knowledge of the Father, just as 1:18 states that it is the only Son who has made the Father known.
Christ is "the image of the invisible God" ([ref:Kol 1:15|Colossians 1:15]). Paul expresses the same idea as John: The invisible God has been made visible through the Son.

God "dwells in unapproachable light, whom no one has ever seen or can see" ([ref:1 Tim 6:16|1 Timothy 6:16]). This confirms the statement in John 1:18 that no one has seen God and underscores the need for the Son's revelation.

The Son is "the radiance of God's glory and the exact representation of his being" ([ref:Heb 1:1-3|Hebrews 1:1-3]). After God spoke in the past through the prophets, he has now spoken through the Son, who fully reveals the Father, as John 1:18 states.

"No one has ever seen God. If we love one another, God lives in us" ([ref:1 Joh 4:12|1 John 4:12]). John repeats the words from the gospel (θεὸν οὐδεὶς πώποτε τεθέαται) and explains how God's invisible presence is made real through love.
